quantity.quote: is a 26-ton water-based neutrino detector at Fermilab on the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB)
The ANNIE detector sits in a 30-meter-deep underground hall on the Fermilab site

name: ANNIE
notes: The Fermilab feature states the ANNIE hall is a 30-meter-deep underground hall on the Fermilab site; the existing campus-grade site is a surface point.

physics_goals.quote: ANNIE is: (1) an important measurement of neutrino-nucleus interactions focusing specifically on neutron production, and (2) an R&D effort focused on using new photodetector technology and chemical additives to make advanced water-base neutrino detectors.
physics_goals.value: Measure the neutron yield of neutrino-nucleus interactions in gadolinium-doped water and test LAPPD photodetectors and water-based liquid scintillator for future neutrino detectors

summary.plain: A 26-tonne tank of gadolinium-doped water in an underground hall at Fermilab, in the Booster neutrino beam, that counts the neutrons knocked out when neutrinos hit oxygen nuclei, and tests ultra-fast light sensors for future neutrino detectors.
summary.technical: Accelerator Neutrino Neutron Interaction Experiment: 26 t water Cherenkov detector (25 t Gd-loaded water target) in the SciBooNE hall on the Booster Neutrino Beam, with PMTs, LAPPDs and a muon range detector; Phase I (2016-17) measured beam neutron backgrounds, Phase II (installed 2019, running 2020) measures final-state neutron multiplicity of CC interactions and tests WbLS and LAPPDs.
